Top candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate first.

This Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato reference (Bugwood_5) shows elongated stem cankers very similar to the test image. Let me check one more bacterial canker reference and also look at a couple more candidates.

Strong match with Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato - the right panel in Bugwood_18 shows an identical elongated whitish/bleached canker on a green tomato stem. I need to check 5 more new classes for coverage.

Based on my analysis:

- **Test image**: Elongated, brown/whitish necrotic canker running longitudinally along a tomato stem, with sunken/splitting tissue
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** (Bugwood_5, Bugwood_18): Both show nearly identical elongated stem cankers — Bugwood_18 right panel is a particularly close visual match with the same elongated whitish lesion on a green hairy tomato stem
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: References showed microscopy and generally necrotic stems, less organized linear canker
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Verticillium_Wilt**: All showed whole-plant wilt/collapse, not localized stem cankers
